title: Adaptive ingress shaping and spot-aware autoscaler for embeddings
creator: Devon Park
description:
Problem: Embeddings ingestion has frequent short-duration bursts from multiple tenants that cause head-of-line queueing, P99 latency spikes, and noisy autoscaler behaviour. The current autoscaler and global rate limiter are too coarse: they either overprovision for sustained throughput or underreact to sudden multi-tenant surges, leading to customer errors and degraded tail latency.

Proposal: Implement an ingress shaping layer plus a spot-aware autoscaler to smooth bursts, provide predictable per-tenant QoS, and improve autoscaler stability. Key components: a) Tenant-aware leaky bucket admission with short-window smoothing; b) Dual-queue admission (short/long embedding jobs) to reduce HOL blocking; c) Hotkey detection and soft-throttling; d) Warm-pool reservation and headroom for short bursts; e) Autoscaler integration that is "spot-aware": treats spot-backed nodes with conservative drain/scale-down cooldowns and cross-nodal headroom reservations.

Goals: Reduce p99 inference latency for embeddings by ~30-50% under bursty traffic, eliminate tail-related 5xx errors during bursts, and reduce autoscaler thrash by 40% (scale events/sec).

Non-goals: This ticket does not change embedding model execution kernels, quantization, or downstream reranking logic. It focuses on ingress/admission, queuing, and scaling orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: Load tests: run burst profile (3x baseline QPS for 30s across 200 tenants) and show p99 latency improvement >= 30% vs current trunk
No increase in p50 latency beyond 1.2x baseline for steady traffic
Autoscaler scale-up/scale-down frequency reduced by >= 40% in synthetic surge tests
New metrics visible on Console: per-tenant admission_rate, short_queue_length, long_queue_length, hotkey_backoff_rate, spot_node_headroom
Canary rollout plan validated: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with safety rollback on error_rate > 0.5%
Docs: runbook and SRE playbook added with troubleshooting links and dashboard queries
tasks: Design: finalize leaky-bucket parameters by SLA tier and short-window smoothing algorithm (Devon, 2d)
Router: implement dual-queue admission + tenant token-bucket with adjustable refill (Maya, 4d)
Hotkey detector: lightweight LRU tracker to identify >90th percentile key traffic and apply soft-throttle (SRE, 3d)
Warm-pool: add headroom reservation API and expose via provisioning service (Infra, 3d)
Autoscaler: add spot-aware scaling rules and conservative drain cooldown (Infra, 5d)
Load testing: create k6/gatling profiles and run comparison tests vs trunk (QA, 3d)
Observability: add metrics + tracing tags; wire dashboards and alerts (Observability, 2d)
Docs + Runbook: write rollout and rollback steps with sample queries (PM, 2d)
Canary rollout and post-mortem: 3-step canary and 72h observation (Maya + SRE)
comments: 2026-02-26 Devon Park: Kickoff — collected customer incidents where embeddings p99 spikes correlated with tenant bursts. Initial analysis shows head-of-line blocking from large-batch requests.

2026-02-28 Maya Gonzalez: Prototype dual-queue admission in dev router. Short-queue prioritizes requests with token_count <= 512. Preliminary results on local cluster: p99 down ~18% under microbursts.
2026-03-01 SRE (Anil Rao): Suggested warm-pool headroom should be configurable per region due to differing spot availability; added dependency on infra-provisioner API change (ENG-99401).

2026-03-03 QA (Jin Lee): Created load profile scripts for 200-tenant burst tests and validated that synthetic hotkeys amplify tail latency. Next step is integrating admission control into load harness.

2026-03-05 Maya Gonzalez: Implemented metric 'hotkey_backoff_rate' and added to embeddings queue dashboard. Observed early canary at 5% reduced p99 by ~23% in staging. Preparing canary plan for next window.
